hook.line: Monday at the café, every regular asks about your weekend. To answer, you need three tiny past forms: where you went, what you did and how it was.
hook.es:
¿Qué hiciste el sábado?
Fui al mercado. Fue un desastre.
hook.en:
What did you do on Saturday?
I went to the market. It was a disaster.

examples.en: On Friday I went to Paloquemao.
What did you do on Saturday? (to a friend)

examples.es: Vale hizo el café, como Rosa.
examples.en: Vale made the coffee, like Rosa.
We went to the cinema last night.
I didn't go to the party.
It was cold in Bogotá yesterday.

examples.es: Hernando y sus amigos fueron al café.
examples.en: Hernando and his friends went to the café.

rule:
Three of the busiest verbs break the past-tense rules you just learned.

*Ir* (to go) and *ser* (to be) share one set of past forms:
*fui*: I went, I was
*fuiste*: you went, you were
*fue*: he, she, you (formal) went or was
*fuimos*: we went, we were
*fueron*: they, you all went or were

The rest of the sentence decides. *Fui al mercado*: a place after *a*, so went. *Fue un desastre*: a description, so was.

*Hacer* (to do, to make): *hice*, *hiciste*, *hizo*, *hicimos*, *hicieron*. Note the *z* in *hizo*. *Hacer* also does the weather: *hizo frío*, it was cold.

None of these carry an accent mark, unlike *compré* or *comió*. And where English needs "did" for a question, Spanish just uses the verb: *¿Qué hiciste?*
smallPrint: Teachers call this tense the preterite (*pretérito indefinido*), and these are its irregular forms. *Ser* and *ir* really do share every one of them.
soundTip: *Fui* is one syllable, close to English *fwee*. *Fue* is one syllable too, like *fweh*. That vowel at the end is the only thing between I and he or she.

options: What did he do last night?
What did you do last night?
What did I do last night?
I went to Medellín with Vale.
I didn't go to the party.
She didn't go to the party.
You didn't go to the party.
Did he go to the market?
Did we go to the market?
Did they go to the market?

yourTurn.prompt: Fill the gap and type the whole sentence: Ayer ___ al mercado. (fui / fue) I went.
yourTurn.why: I went is *fui*; *fue* is he or she.

yourTurn.prompt: Fill the gap and type the whole sentence: El sábado ___ un desastre. (fui / fue) Saturday was a disaster.
yourTurn.why: The day is an it, so *fue*.

yourTurn.prompt: Fill the gap and type the whole sentence: ¿Qué ___ anoche? (hizo / hiciste) Asking a friend.
yourTurn.why: To a friend, you did is *hiciste*.

yourTurn.prompt: We went to Monserrate on Sunday.
Make it about we: Fui al mercado.
Make it negative: Hice el café.
Ask Don Hernando, politely: What did you do on Sunday?
yourTurn.why: With *usted*, it's the he and she form: *hizo*.

yourTurn.prompt: Now it's two people: Vale fue al parque. Make it Vale and Tomás.
yourTurn.answer: Vale y Tomás fueron al parque.

pitfalls.why: Almost. *Fue* is he or she; for I it's *fui*.
Close. These short forms carry no accent mark: *fui*, *fue*.
Nearly. *Hacer* is irregular in the past: it's *hizo*, with a *z*.

personal: What did you do last weekend? Write three sentences: where you went (*fui*), something you did (*hice*) and how it was (*fue*).
